label: Median standard of living

fields.name: revenu_median
fields.label: Median standard of living (disposable income per consumption unit)

fields.name: revenu_d1
fields.label: 1st decile — the poorest tenth are below this

fields.name: revenu_d9
fields.label: 9th decile — the richest tenth are above this

legend_note: Disposable income after taxes and benefits, per consumption unit, so household size is accounted for. The national median commune sits at €22,810 and the scale diverges around it: brown is below, teal above. Published for 31,157 communes covering 99.6% of the population. This is where people live, not where they work.

label: Income inequality (D9/D1 ratio)
legend_note: How many times richer the top tenth is than the bottom tenth. Median commune 2.8. Grey is not equality — it is INSEE statistical secrecy: the ratio is published for only 5,253 communes, because a small commune's deciles would identify households. Those communes still hold 76.8% of the population.

label: Poverty rate

fields.name: taux_pauvrete
fields.label: Share living below 60% of the national median

legend_note: Share of people under 60% of the national median standard of living — the standard European poverty line. Median commune 12%. Published for 4,306 communes holding 73% of the population; everywhere else is withheld as too small, not poverty-free.
